name: Francis Hamilton
notable_stories: Best friend of Scottish poet Robert Burns
His brother Alexander fled from Prince George's County to Keeptrist in 1777.
milestones: Buried: No burial site has been found
locations: Shepherdstown area, along the Potomac River
Keeptrist, Berkeley Co., VA (now Jefferson Co., WV)
sources: Further Research on the Family and Descendants of Joseph P. and Elizabeth (Hamilton) Adams, William W. Allen (February 2012)
notes: Father of Elizabeth (Eliza) Hamilton (wife of Jose Pierre Adams). Parents: John Hamilton of Kype and Jacobina Young.
CORRECTION 2026-09-23: Death refined from "c. 1802" to "abt 1802" [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9170].

Left a will, but it was recorded in a lost book of Berkeley Co.; heirs are named in the court suit North vs. the heirs of Francis HAMILTON, in brother Alexander's will, and in grandson Francis Alexander HAMILTON's will [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9181]
Witnessed a lease from Joseph McCormick Mason to John Semple for 400 acres; must have been in America by 1765 [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9186]
Appointed with Thomas Hart, Henry Lloyd and Godwin Smith to view ground for a road from Semples Furnace to the Warm Springs Road [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9190]
Bought from John Keys for 35 pounds a bay horse, a feather bed and furniture, and a share in a 1769 tobacco crop [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9193]
John Semple, indebted to him, conveyed cows, furniture and grain to him [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9199]
Slave owner, taxed in 1774 for slaves Peter, Roger, Sarah, Beck, Jeremiah and Thomas [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9201]
Listed at the sale of Abraham Buckle's estate [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9202]
Witnessed the will of Barbara Merriotes (Merritt?) [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9203]
Bought Lot 42 in Sharpsburg from Michael Taylor for 2 pounds [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9204]
One of the executors of the will of Andrew Telleroy [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9206]

In 1782-1787 paid tax on 1 poll and 5 slaves in Berkeley Co.; named in audits of John Creighton's (19 Mar 1782) and Robert T. Tabb's (20 Aug 1782) estates and attended the sale of Barbara Merritt's estate [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9207]
David Meek's will left 10 pounds to Francis HAMILTON of Berkeley Co. [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9196]

Taxed on 4 white males 16-21, 7 blacks above 16, 12 blacks under 16 and 13 horses in the district of Commissioner Thomas Hart; neighbors included David Evans, the Hagelys, the Houtes, Henry Jacob, John Moler, Elizabeth Rianer and John Womandorf [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9210]
Named in the settlement of George Adam MOLER's estate, and in the 2nd settlement on 21 Jan 1793 [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9216]
Bought 123 acres in Berkeley Co. from Henry Lee of Stafford Co., VA [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9217]
Witnessed the will of Isaac Strider [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9219]
Bought 120 acres from Peter Fleck, previously owned by Charles Friend [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9220]
Three estate records exist in Jefferson Co. (pages missing); property distributed to heirs on 20 Apr 1809 [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9223]
